+class FileLock:
+    """An exclusive flock held on an open lock file; a context manager that releases it."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fd):
+        self._fd = fd
+
+    def release(self):
+        """Unlock and close the lock file; calling it again does nothing."""
+        fd, self._fd = self._fd, None
+        if fd is None:
+            return
+        try:
+            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+
+    def __enter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, *exc_info):
+        self.release()

+def _open_lock_file(name):
+    """Open (creating if missing) the lock file and return its descriptor.
+
+    flock needs no write access, so an existing lock file this user may not

2\. Replacing a lock permits lost updates 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
_open_lock_file opens the current lock pathname and lock() flocks that descriptor without
ensuring later writers will open the same inode. In a shared directory, an owner of a pre-planted
lock entry can replace it while one writer holds it, allowing a second writer to enter the
read–modify–write sequence under a different lock.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Replacing an attacker-owned lock entry lets two writers flock different inodes while changing the same data file. ## Fix Focus Areas - todo/store.py[41-47] - todo/store.py[73-86] - todo/store.py[102-108] ## Recommended Fix Use a lock location whose directory entries cannot be replaced by another writer, and reject symlink or non-regular lock entries. Add a test that replaces a pre-planted lock entry while the first process holds its descriptor and verifies that the second cannot enter. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
